purpose: Illustrative teaching examples, not measured tool output

prompts.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: educational illustration for an offline design handbook for a backend engineer.
Primary request: show the SAME invoice-management web app before and after a thoughtful design cleanup. Make the actual visual differences unmistakable, with large readable UI and numbered explanatory callouts. This is a fictional teaching example, not a measured tool output.
Composition: wide landscape 3:2 canvas, two equally sized browser-window panels side by side, generous margins. Left heading exactly "BEFORE: hard to scan". Right heading exactly "AFTER: clear next action". Main page title in both: "Invoices". Both screens contain the same three invoice rows, the same information, the same actions. Invoice rows: "INV-104  Acme  $240  Paid", "INV-105  North  $480  Overdue", "INV-106  Field  $120  Draft". Action names "New invoice", "Export", "Filter".
Left: realistic but messy beginner UI: crowded irregular spacing, equally emphasized Export and New invoice, cramped row alignment, little heading hierarchy, status is only a small unlabeled colored dot (keep the visible text status labels only on right). Avoid caricature; still recognizably functional.
Right: carefully arranged practical business UI, prominent page title, one filled teal New invoice action, secondary Export outlined, Filter near table, aligned columns and currency, airy consistent spacing, status badges use both color and readable Paid/Overdue/Draft words.
Around the right panel show four numbered small callout circles with short captions placed OUTSIDE the UI and connected cleanly:
"1  One primary action"
"2  Related things stay together"
"3  Aligned rows scan faster"
"4  Color plus words"
Style: precise flat editorial vector-inspired illustration, subtle paper white background, deep ink navy text, muted teal and warm terracotta accents. Render all UI text legibly. Little decoration, no people, no logos, no watermarks, no code. Use the illustrations to explain the change, do not merely illustrate abstract stages. Title at top exactly "Same data. Easier decisions."

Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: educational illustration for an offline design handbook for a backend engineer.
Primary request: explain visually the difference between a marketing website and a working application. Two equal browser mockups, wide landscape 3:2 canvas. No preference implied; different jobs require different designs. Large readable text, clear examples.
Title exactly "First, choose the job."
Left heading "MARKETING WEBSITE". Below a polished fictional developer-product website. Its hero text exactly "Ship invoices in minutes." with one button "Try the API". A restrained editorial illustration of connected invoices is secondary to the headline. Below are three small feature summaries represented by short line shapes. Caption below the browser: "Help someone decide to try it." Tool label below caption: "Start: Taste Skill". Small optional sublabel: "Reference: getdesign.md".
Right heading "WORKING APPLICATION". Below a practical fictional invoice-management app with small sidebar, title "Invoices", action "New invoice", a compact filter strip, table with three rows, status badges, and one empty-state miniature panel inset beside it. Clear visual hierarchy, no marketing hero. Caption below browser: "Help someone finish a task." Tool label below caption: "Start: Impeccable".
At bottom a single shared horizontal band with exactly "Both: review with Web Design Guidelines".
Style: flat editorial illustration, warm paper white, ink navy, teal and terracotta accents; highly readable, minimal decoration, matching visual grammar across both panels. No logos, no claims of measured improvement. No extra text beyond provided labels and minimal readable generic invoice table labels.
